_about: Field terms for F32, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

proper-scoring-rule.definition: a score for probability forecasts on which a forecaster does best in expectation by stating their true belief
proper-scoring-rule.excludes: scores that pay for shading a forecast toward some answer, and any rule for which questions to answer

brier.definition: the squared difference between the stated probabilities and the outcomes, here summed over the answer options in the GJP form so it runs from 0 to 2; lower is better
brier.excludes: questions left unanswered, which it does not score

selective-prediction.definition: prediction with a reject option, where a system answers only the inputs it ranks most likely to be right and declines the rest
selective-prediction.excludes: how the kept answers are produced

risk-coverage.definition: the error on kept items against the share kept; here risk is the mean Brier score of kept forecasts and coverage the share kept
risk-coverage.excludes: any score for the forecasts withheld

extremising.definition: pushing a probability away from 50 percent by multiplying its log-odds by a factor a, with a below 1 pulling it inward instead
extremising.excludes: changing which side a forecast leans to

cc0.definition: the Creative Commons public domain dedication, under which anyone may reuse the work for any purpose without permission
cc0.excludes: a licence condition requiring citation, which stays a scholarly courtesy

prediction-market.definition: a market in which people trade contracts that pay on an outcome, with the price read as a probability
prediction-market.excludes: the individual survey forecasts analysed in this paper

sha-256.definition: a hash function that turns a file into a 64-character fingerprint which changes if any byte changes; a recorded hash shows the file was not altered after it was taken
sha-256.excludes: encryption, because the hash keeps nothing secret and cannot be turned back into the file

voided-question.definition: a question the tournament cancelled without scoring, so no forecast on it has an outcome
voided-question.excludes: a void verdict in our sense, which concerns a failed planted check or a sample below its minimum

superteam.definition: a team made up of forecasters drawn from the top performers of the previous tournament year (condition 5)
superteam.excludes: ordinary teams (condition 4), formed without selection on past accuracy

skip.definition: a closed question that was open during a forecaster's active window in a year and that they never answered, inferred from the data
skip.excludes: questions outside the active window, and any recorded decision to decline, which the data do not hold

relative-brier.definition: a forecaster's mean, over the questions they answered, of their first-forecast Brier score minus the median first-forecast Brier score on that question; lower is better
relative-brier.excludes: the difficulty of the question, which subtracting the median removes

forecaster-year.definition: one person's forecasts within one tournament year, the unit for skip rate and relative score
forecaster-year.excludes: pooling of different people, and pooling one person's years

stratum.definition: a group of units alike on the matched variables, here year and twentieth of forecast count, inside which a statistic is computed before averaging
stratum.excludes: control for variables that were not matched

spearman.definition: the correlation between the ranks of two quantities, from -1 to +1, which reads any steady rise or fall
spearman.excludes: the shape of the relation and the pull of outliers on the raw values

bootstrap.definition: recomputing a number many times on data resampled with replacement, here within strata or over questions, to see how much it varies
bootstrap.excludes: an interval from a textbook formula that assumes a distribution

log-odds.definition: for a probability p, the natural log of p divided by 1 minus p; 0 at 50 percent and unbounded toward certainty
log-odds.excludes: any information beyond the probability, of which it is a rescaling

held-out.definition: the drop in Brier score from extremising, with the factor fitted on one half of the questions and scored on the other half
held-out.excludes: the in-sample improvement any fitted factor gives on the data it was fitted to

out-of-fold.definition: a prediction for each item made from a fit on the other folds only
out-of-fold.excludes: any use of the item's own outcome to predict it

aurc.definition: the mean risk over coverages from 10 to 100 percent in steps of 5, one number for a whole filter; lower is better

positive-control.definition: a test of an effect already known to be present, which the instrument must detect for its other readings to be trusted
positive-control.excludes: a shuffle control, which removes an effect instead

test-retest.definition: the correlation between one person's value in one year and the same person's value in the next, a measure of how stable the quantity is
test-retest.excludes: change caused by anything the person did between the two years

ece.definition: the gap between stated probability and hit rate, averaged over probability bins and weighted by bin size; folded here by taking each forecast on the side it leans to
ece.excludes: how informative forecasts are, since a forecast of the base rate every time can score zero
